{{Short description|none}}
{{Use Canadian English|date=January 2023}}
The Canadian territory of [[Nunavut]] was formed on April 1, 1999, through the ''[[Nunavut Act]]'' and the [[Nunavut Land Claims Agreement Act]]. Nunavut, since its formation, has had a [[consensus government]]. In a consensus government, the premier is elected by the non-partisan members of the Legislative Assembly. Prior to April 1, 1999, the land that Nunavut occupies was part of the [[Northwest Territories]].<ref>{{cite web|accessdate=10 November 2008|url=http://archives.cbc.ca/politics/provincial_territorial_politics/topics/1155/|title=On the Nunavut Campaign Trail |publisher=CBC }}</ref>

==History==
{{see also|Premier of Nunavut}}
The territory's first premier, [[Paul Okalik]], was elected after the [[1999 Nunavut general election|1999 general election]]. He was re-elected to a second term after the [[2004 Nunavut general election|2004 general election]].<ref>{{cite web|accessdate=10 November 2008|url=http://www.cbc.ca/nunavutvotes2008/riding/009/index.html|title=Constituency Profiles |publisher=CBC|date=27 October 2008 }}</ref> Although Okalik was re-elected to a third term after the [[2008 Nunavut general election|2008 general election]] in the [[Iqaluit West]] riding, he was defeated by newly elected MLA [[Eva Aariak]] in the premiership vote on November 14.<ref>[https://www.theglobeandmail.com/servlet/story/RTGAM.20081114.wnunavutpremier1115/BNStory/National/home "Nunavut names new premier"] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081117011937/http://www.theglobeandmail.com/servlet/story/RTGAM.20081114.wnunavutpremier1115/BNStory/National/home |date=2008-11-17 }}, ''[[The Globe and Mail]]'', November 14, 2008.</ref> On November 15, 2013, [[Peter Taptuna]] beat out Paul Okalik and [[Paul Quassa]] for the position of premier.<ref>[http://www.nunatsiaqonline.ca/stories/article/65674mlas_choose_xxxxxx_to_serve_as_nunavut_premier/ MLAs choose Peter Taptuna to serve as Nunavut premier]</ref>
